sources.description:
Portrait of Ho Ka Kui

Ho Ka Kui, celebrated as Hong Kong cinema’s quintessential villain, built a prolific career with over 400 film appearances. His intense performances in movies like "Prison on Fire" and "School on Fire" cemented his reputation as the industry’s "King of Villains."

Off-screen, Ho Ka Kui faced severe personal challenges. A gambling addiction cost him his fortune multiple times, and a battle with diabetes forced him to retire early. When he died in 2015 at 66, he had only a few hundred dollars left and no family at his side. His enduring film legacy continues to captivate audiences.

Known for his iconic villain roles in over 300 Hong Kong films, He Jiaju earned acclaim for his performance as “Big Mi” in the 1987 movie “Prison,” which garnered him a Best Supporting Actor nomination at the 7th Hong Kong Film Awards. Ho Ka-Kui: Hong Kong’s Iconic Villain

Ho Ka-Kui earned renown in Hong Kong cinema as one of the "Four Great Villains," delivering chilling performances in crime and action films. His intense portrayal of a perverse character in "Rebels of the Neon God" cemented his reputation for bringing complex antagonists to life.

Off-screen, Ho Ka-Kui faced personal demons, including drug addiction and compulsive gambling. These struggles depleted his finances and left him living in isolation.
